summary: Hamilton County, Tennessee lookout run by the Division of Forestry; staffed into 2014 and described as safe to climb in 2019.

facts.design: Traditional Aermotor-style tower, 80 feet tall, with a 7 by 7 foot cab and wooden steps

access.note: Beside the Division of Forestry office. The 2019 Register entry says guests may climb, but confirm with the office before going up.

events.note: Frank Westwood staffed the tower into 2014; the Register does not say when staffing ended
2019 Register entry: good condition and safe to climb
Registered February 19, 2019 as US 1292, TN 33; nominated by Victoria Oliver

evidence.supports: administered by Tennessee Division of Forestry
traditional Aermotor-style tower, 80 feet tall, 7x7 cab, wooden steps
evidence.quote: It is a traditional Aermotor style tower, 80' tall, with 7'x7' cab and wooden steps.

evidence.supports: one of 28 fire towers in the Chattanooga District
evidence.quote: At one time, Montlake was one of 28 fire towers in the Chattanooga District.

evidence.supports: towers in sight of each other, watching jointly
evidence.quote: They were all in sight of each other, watching jointly over thousands of acres of land.

evidence.supports: Jim Brown manned 17 years; Frank Westwood into 2014
evidence.quote: The tower was manned for 17 years by forestry technician Jim Brown, and into 2014 by Frank Westwood.

evidence.supports: good condition and safe to climb in 2019
evidence.quote: The lookout is in good condition, and was safe to climb in 2019.

evidence.supports: next to forestry office; guests allowed to climb
evidence.quote: The tower is located next to the forestry office, which allows guests to climb the tower.

notes_for_editor: Two sources. The NHLR entry is detailed on staffing and the 2019 condition; tnlandforms confirms standing and elevation. Nothing dated after 2019. The register dates the build only to the 1950s, so no built event was entered. The one web search found nothing about this tower. The OpenStreetMap node in the brief was not read. The permission access level is my reading of allows guests to climb the tower; confirm with the office. No photos added; the NHLR photo is already in the record.
